conditions: Select local non-SSO browser customers using primary hosted AuthKit in staging. This is not AuthKit Connect, Directory Sync, native/mobile, brokered workforce or the standalone SMS MFA API.

Hosted MFA uses authenticator-app TOTP. Required mode covers new and existing non-SSO users, but a configurable method is not an observed mandatory policy. TOTP is not equivalent to phishing resistance.

SSO users are exempt from hosted MFA. Organization MFA applies to the selected organization for non-SSO members: https://workos.com/docs/authkit/organization-policies. Effective environment/organization settings and user context remain unverified.

Staging is offered for no-cost testing: https://workos.com/docs/authkit/environments. Account entitlement, quotas and future costs are unverified; production billing, enterprise connections and paid custom domains are not included. No account, subscription, credential, enrollment, environment or policy was created.

evidence.summary: The hosted AuthKit guide documents configurable TOTP MFA and Required mode for non-SSO users. OPTIONAL is a mechanism proposal, not observed compulsory use, SSO coverage or verified account entitlement.

conditions: Availability is a conditional mechanism-level inference from domain-bound WebAuthn passkeys, not every login or all MFA. Bind the intended HTTPS WorkOS staging RP/domain and validate the authenticator and browser; user verification is documented, not observed.

Progressive enrollment is off by default and can be skipped, including future reminders. Required MFA accepts a passkey with user verification instead of a separate TOTP challenge; this is not a passkey-only policy or a hardware-key/AAL guarantee.

Password, Magic Auth and TOTP alternatives need independent policy review. Enrollment, password reset, recovery, administrator credential removal and existing SSO/session paths do not establish complete journey protection; enforcement remains UNKNOWN.

Staging uses WorkOS domains; custom domains are production-only: https://workos.com/docs/authkit/environments. Domain migration can invalidate credentials. No paid domain was selected. Seven earlier WorkOS scopes, AuthWeave's ZITADEL/BFF and synthetic evaluator are unchanged.

evidence.summary: The hosted passkey guide documents WebAuthn, domain binding, skippable enrollment and user verification satisfying MFA. Mechanism availability is conditional; mandatory customer-journey phishing protection remains UNKNOWN.

conditions: The Widgets API documents passkey registration options and verification but does not establish a hardware-only attestation policy for this hosted-login staging scope. A passkey label, biometric/PIN or user verification is not proof of a non-exportable private key.

Synced, cross-device, existing credential and recovery paths require independent key-protection review. Trusted authenticator metadata, key protection and enforceable enrollment restrictions are unverified; keep both fields UNKNOWN, not provider-wide UNSUPPORTED.

Hosted login and authenticated Widgets account management are distinct surfaces. Widgets registration/deletion require elevatedAccessToken; the token name and opaque registration options do not certify stronger authentication or hardware protection. No Widgets integration, attestation validation, purchase or physical-device test occurred.

evidence.summary: The Widgets API describes registration/verification and elevated-token account management, not verified hardware-only key protection in hosted AuthKit staging. Non-exportable availability and enforcement remain UNKNOWN.

conditions: The reauthentication guide documents max_age and an access-token auth_time advanced by active authentication, not refresh. AuthKit chooses a password, MFA factor or upstream SSO method; fresh sign-in alone does not establish requesting and verifying stronger authentication.

The project defines step-up as stronger authentication, not repeating the same login. No selected stronger-factor contract or essential-ACR higher-assurance enforcement is verified for primary AuthKit staging; availability remains UNKNOWN, not provider-wide UNSUPPORTED.

Independently validate signed issuer/audience/expiry, session/user and callback state binding, auth_time and required factor freshness at the sensitive-operation gate. Missing, malformed, future or insufficient evidence must deny; a decoded timestamp, token refresh or UI redirect is not operation authorization.

The guide's step-up terminology describes recency, not automatic NIST AAL, hardware protection or Keycloak LoA. No protected operation, challenge, token validation or bypass test was executed. Stronger-factor enforcement stays UNKNOWN; no Connect or standalone MFA API behavior is inherited.

evidence.summary: The guide documents recent reauthentication with max_age/auth_time and provider-selected methods, which can include password re-entry. A stronger-factor request/proof and sensitive-operation gate are unverified; both fields remain UNKNOWN.
